name: restore-point
desc: Free, open-source restore point manager for Windows — create, schedule and compare system checkpoints offline. 100 MB portable, MIT.
features: ✅ **One-click checkpoint** — create a named restore point in seconds without digging through System Protection
✅ **Auto-schedule** — daily, pre-update or before each detected driver install
✅ **Comparison browser** — list points with age, size and the events each one precedes
✅ **Retention policy** — cap by count or disk percentage so points never eat the whole drive
✅ **Protection status panel** — shows which drives have protection enabled and fixes the disabled ones
✅ **Restore from app or boot** — trigger the rollback directly, or export the instructions for WinRE
✅ **100 MB self-contained exe** — runtime bundled, portable, offline, MIT with SHA-256 releases
compare: | Feature | **restore-point** | Restore Point Creator | System Protection | EaseUS Todo Free |
| Named one-click points | **Yes** | Yes | Partial | n/a imaging |
| Scheduling with policies | **Yes** | Task scripted | No | Partial |
| Disk usage caps by percent | **Yes** | No | Yes | n/a
| Portable, no install | **Yes, 100 MB** | Installer | With OS | Installer |
faqQ: how to create restore points automatically on Windows 10 and 11?
faqA: System Protection is off by default on many systems and its dialog hides frequency, naming and storage caps. restore-point turns checkpoints into a first-class tool: one-click creation, scheduled snapshots before updates and a retention policy that respects disk space. It is a 100 MB portable exe, MIT, offline.
s1: Dark timeline (#121418, amber #F59E0B): restore points arranged by date with names and suspected triggers, Create point button top right, disk usage bar at 3 percent.
s2: Comparison list: two points selected with event chips (driver install, audit week), size and age columns, delete older action.
s3: Protection panel: system drive enabled green, data drive disabled with fix action, retention policy dropdown keep 4 percent of disk.
